facts.system_prompt: You are a scriptwriter for viral YouTube Shorts in the 'Did You Know' niche. Every video is a single surprising, verifiable fact. You write punchy hooks, use concrete numbers, and never exaggerate. Only state facts you are highly confident are true and widely documented. If unsure, pick a different fact. Avoid anything that could be misinformation.
topics: octopus has three hearts and blue blood
honey never spoils if stored properly
bananas are radioactive enough to trigger some detectors
sharks existed before trees
the Eiffel Tower grows about 15 cm taller in summer
a day on Venus is longer than its year
cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the Great Pyramid
there are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way
your body contains enough iron to make a 3-inch nail
wombat poop is cube-shaped
the human nose can distinguish over a trillion scents
hot water can freeze faster than cold water (Mpemba effect)
a teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh a billion tons
bacteria outnumber human cells in your body roughly 1.3 to 1
the Sahara desert is roughly the size of the United States
lightning strikes Earth about 100 times every second
the deepest part of the ocean is deeper than Everest is tall
a cloud can weigh over a million pounds
there is a species of jellyfish that is biologically immortal
the first computer bug was a literal moth

explainers.system_prompt: You are a scriptwriter for educational explainer Shorts. You break down one concept in under 60 seconds: setup, key mechanism, payoff. Use simple analogies. Never use jargon without immediately defining it.
topics: how compound interest actually works
what a blockchain really is
how vaccines train the immune system
why the sky is blue (Rayleigh scattering)
how GPS knows where you are
what dark matter is and isn't
how noise-cancelling headphones work
why we dream (current theories)
how mRNA vaccines differ from traditional ones
what a black hole actually is
how the stock market sets prices
why planes can fly (Bernoulli is not the whole story)
how your phone battery degrades
what inflation really means
how CRISPR edits genes
why antibiotic resistance happens

stories.system_prompt: You are a narrator for true, atmospheric short stories drawn from real history, science, or strange events. Tone: cinematic, calm, slightly suspenseful. Never invent facts — stick to verifiable events. End with a short reflective line.
topics: the Dyatlov Pass incident
the disappearance of the Roanoke colony
the dancing plague of 1518
the last message from the Franklin expedition
the Antikythera mechanism
the wow signal of 1977
the Voynich manuscript
the Somerton Man mystery
the Mary Celeste ghost ship
the Taos Hum
the Bloop underwater sound
the Bermuda Triangle's real history
